concerns.text: Task T090b is marked `[P]` (parallel‑safe) but declares a dependency on T090. `[P]` tasks must have no explicit dependencies.
Task T091 is marked `[P]` yet depends on T090b, violating the parallel‑safe contract.
Task T091-Check is marked `[P]` but lists a dependency on T091, which makes it non‑parallel‑safe.
Task T004-Verify is tagged `[P]` while depending on T004; this contradicts the definition of `[P]`.
Task T008 is marked `[P]` yet depends on T007, so it cannot safely run in parallel with other tasks.
Task T014 (counterbalancing) is labeled `[P]` but has an explicit `Depends on: T013`, breaking the parallel‑safe guarantee.
Task T015 (random presentation order) carries `[P]` while depending on T014, which makes the tag inaccurate.
Task T010a is marked `[P]` but lists a dependency on T013, violating the parallel‑safe semantics.
Task T051 is tagged `[P]` yet depends on T015b-Real, so it cannot be run in parallel with its producer.
Task T086 is marked `[P]` but depends on T051, making the `[P]` annotation incorrect.
Task T101 is labeled `[P]` while depending on three prior tasks (T051, T086, T015c-Guard); this breaks the parallel‑safe contract.
Task T021 (primary LMM script) consumes `analysis_ready.csv` produced by T020 but does not declare a dependency on T020, creating a producer‑before‑consumer ordering violation.
Task T013 (stimulus generation) runs before foundational tasks T001 (project structure) and T005 (directory creation), so required directories may not exist when the script executes.
Task T014 (counterbalancing) also precedes T001/T005, risking missing directories or config files needed for file output.
Task T015 (random order) is scheduled before the project‑structure tasks (T001/T005), violating the required producer‑consumer order.
Task T124 implements the pre‑analysis guard but the accompanying test T125, which depends on T124, is listed after it without an explicit dependency, leading to a potential ordering gap.
Task T112 (straight‑lining contract test) is placed before its producer T016a, so the test could run before the artifact it validates exists.
Task T113 (power‑analysis JSON contract test) appears before the power‑analysis generation task T091, breaking the producer‑consumer sequence.
Task T126 (mock‑guard test) is listed before the guard implementation T124/T125, creating a reverse dependency.
Task T127 (no‑fallback test) is scheduled prior to the data‑loading scripts it validates, resulting in an ordering violation.
